# The Examination

Dr. Sarah Chen held her breath as she guided the tiny camera forward.

"You're doing great, Mrs. Patterson," she said, her eyes fixed on the monitor. "Just a little further."

The colonoscopy had been routine until now. But there—on the screen—something moved.

"What the..." Sarah leaned closer.

The creature was no larger than a grain of rice, pale and segmented, undulating against the intestinal wall. A parasitic worm, likely *Enterobius vermicularis*—a common pinworm, though she'd need lab confirmation.

"Mrs. Patterson, I'm seeing something here. Have you experienced any itching? Disrupted sleep?"

The patient's voice came muffled from beneath the sedation's haze. "My daughter's preschool had an outbreak last month..."

Sarah nodded, already mentally drafting the treatment plan. Mebendazole for the whole family, thorough cleaning protocols, the standard reassurances that this was common, treatable, nothing to be embarrassed about.

She captured several images for the file and began the careful withdrawal of the scope.

"The good news," she said, stripping off her gloves afterward, "is that this is one of the easiest things we treat. Two doses of medication, and you'll be completely clear."

Mrs. Patterson sighed with relief.

Just another Tuesday in gastroenterology.
